metadata.name: fork_formation_threshold
metadata.description:
Fork Formation Threshold Sweep

PURPOSE: Determine at what violation rate (fraction of v26 blocks that violate v27
rules) a chainsplit forms and sustains, versus heals organically.

Prior sweep (softfork_rule_strength) assumed a structural partition from block 0
and measured fork *resolution*. This sweep starts both partitions on the same chain
tip (partition_mode=unified) and measures fork *formation*: does the v26-produced
chain diverge far enough to sustain, or do compliant blocks pull the chains back
together before the retarget fires?

The primary outcome is fork_convergence.healed (True/False). At low violation rates
compliant blocks dominate and the fork heals. At high violation rates violating blocks
accumulate faster than the cross-submitted compliant blocks can overcome. The
threshold violation rate is the main result.

RESEARCH QUESTION:
  At what violation rate does a chainsplit form and sustain at all?
  How does committed hashrate (C) affect that threshold?

DESIGN:
- 10 violation rates (0.05–1.00) x 3 C values (0.30, 0.40, 0.50) x 3 replications
- 90 scenarios total, 8 per namespace (6 with 8, 6 with 7), 12 namespaces (6/server)
- Network: lite, partition_mode=unified (both sides start on same chain tip)
- Duration: 13000s with --fork-heal-exit (exits early when chains converge)
- E fixed at 0.65, hashrate fixed at 0.25 (same as all prior sweeps)

KEY VIOLATION RATES (p = 1 - violation_rate):
  0.05 (p=0.95) — almost all blocks compliant; fork should heal quickly
  0.10 (p=0.90) — 10% violating; near-unified chains
  0.15 (p=0.85) — 15% violating; expected to heal
  0.20 (p=0.80) — 20% violating; approaching threshold zone
  0.25 (p=0.75) — 25% violating; threshold candidate
  0.30 (p=0.70) — 30% violating; threshold candidate
  0.40 (p=0.60) — 40% violating; likely to sustain
  0.50 (p=0.50) — 50% violating; symmetric contention
  0.75 (p=0.25) — 75% violating; peak v27 success in prior sweep
  1.00 (p=0.00) — strict UASF baseline; always sustains

SERVER SPLIT:
  Server 1: namespaces fft-0 to fft-5 (sweep_0000–sweep_0044)
  Server 2: namespaces fft-0 to fft-5 (sweep_0045–sweep_0089)

NEW OUTCOME FIELDS (vs softfork_rule_strength):
  fork_convergence.healed        — True if chains converged organically
  fork_convergence.heal_time_s   — Elapsed seconds at convergence
  fork_convergence.v27_blocks_at_heal
  fork_convergence.v26_blocks_at_heal
